headline: Law extends three U.S. Geological Survey water-tracking programs through 2028 and updates rules for federal stream gauges.
what_it_does: This law renews three U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) programs through fiscal year 2028: the Federal Priority Streamgage program, which measures water flow in major rivers and streams; a groundwater monitoring program, including the National Groundwater Monitoring Network; and grants for new ways to estimate, measure, and monitor water. It renames the National Streamflow Information Program as the Federal Priority Streamgage program. It requires that the water-quality sensors on stream gauges be precipitation water-quality sensors. It also requires each gauge site to match federal needs identified through regular outreach and feedback, such as a 2022 USGS report on program priorities.

who_it_affects.how: The agency is authorized to keep running these water monitoring and grant programs through 2028 and must follow new rules for gauge sensors and site selection.

who_it_affects.group: Groups that apply for water technology grants
who_it_affects.how: Grants for developing water estimation, measurement, and monitoring tools remain authorized through 2028.

who_it_affects.group: People and agencies that rely on flood and drought data
who_it_affects.how: Stream and groundwater monitoring that tracks water levels and conditions like floods and droughts continues under the renewed programs.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; programs are reauthorized through fiscal year 2028.
